# Numbers and names

How a typed number is kept and shown, which numbers are questioned, and how two goals or two people with the same name are told apart.

## The rule

One rule for every way in: the check-in, New goal, goal edit, the workspace set-up, the spreadsheet import and the AI tools (backlog N).

**Never rounded quietly.** Each number goal keeps a number of decimal places (*Decimals*, 0 to 3), and every number of it is shown at those places. A number typed with more (`typedDecimals`: the digits after the point, trailing zeros not counted; a decimal comma counts as a point) is refused (`precisionProblem`), saying what it would show as and the two ways forward: type it at the goal's places, or raise Decimals. In a check-in the refusal offers to raise Decimals for the goal in one step, to the places the number was typed with, up to 3 (`placesToKeep`: "Keep 1 decimal place for this goal"), logged as a change to the goal with why. This holds for a check-in's value, a start, target, limit, margin and any plan number typed by hand. A plan already stored isn't judged again when a goal is edited; only numbers changed are. An import that adds a goal without Decimals takes the most decimal places its start, target and limit were typed with (up to 3).

**Letters in a number** get one message everywhere (`notNumberText`): ““a12” isn't a number. Type digits only, like 29.4.” Its example is at the goal's decimal places when there is a goal (`exampleNumber`): “like 29” for whole numbers, “like 29.45” for two places. (Letters after the digits are read as a unit: “12 days” is 12.)

**Thousands grouped.** Every number shown is written at its places with its thousands grouped by commas (`groupDigits`, `fixed`): 1,250,000; −12,000; 1,250.5. Files and the AI tools' data carry the plain number.

**Questioned, never refused.** In a check-in, see [the check-in](check-in.md). Setting a goal up, the questions are [goal entry](goal-entry.md)'s rule 3 (`goalChecks`), the same at every door: below zero for a percentage, time or money; over 100%; a target 100 times the start or more, or a 100th of it or less (both non-zero, the same sign); a billion or more; each that applies, not only the first. A goal already set up that way isn't asked again.

**Plan changes confirmed, never silent** (`planQuestion`). The same check as a check-in's, applied when an existing number goal's plan changes, in the app's goal edit, the spreadsheet import, the data tables and the AI tools (one rule, in the change engine and the edit form). Two things are asked, in this order, and the change saves only once someone says yes:
- **Which way is better flips:** the new target is on the other side of the start (a 14 → 3 min goal given a target of 999). It says so: “This makes higher better: the target (999 min) is now above the start (14 min). It was 14 min to 3 min, lower is better.” The yes is “Yes, make higher better”.
- **Far outside the old plan:** a new start, target or hand-set week's number more than 2 times the old plan's width beyond either end (`farOutside`): “The target of 400% is far outside the plan it replaces (30% to 75%). Status, progress and the forecast will all be judged against it.”

The app asks under the target, in the Check block, as goal entry's rule 3 (`direction`, `far-from-plan`); Import and Data list the questions above What will change with one yes button; the AI tools refuse with the question until called again with `confirm: true`. A plan already stored isn't asked about again.

**Names.** A workspace's, a goal's or an outcome's name has at least 3 characters (`nameProblem`). Two goals may have the same title (compared without case or outer spaces): making one warns (`sameTitleNote`), and wherever both could be on screen each shows its key, or else its team, beside the title (`duplicateTitles`, `goalTell`). An import row with no key whose title another goal has is that goal again unless it names another team; then it's a new goal, noted. Two people may have the same name: the email is who someone is. Adding or renaming one says so (`sameNameNote`); beside the name goes their team, else their job title, else their email, whichever tells them apart (`personTell`). Each avatar's colour comes from the person's ID, and people with the same initials each get a colour none of the others has while there are colours to go round (`avatarHues`, 6 colours).

## Limits the records hold

Faro’s database holds these as well as the rule; a rebuild holds them wherever it stores the records. The constraint names are in `spec/core/schema.sql`, which is for reading, not copying.

- A goal’s key is “G-” and a whole number from 1, with no leading zero (G-1, G-27). (`okr_goals_key_check`; the code holds it too, in `src/domain/goalKey.ts`)
- Keys are given from one counter per workspace that only goes up, starting after 0, so a key is never given twice, even after its goal is removed. Give them in one place, the server. (`okr_goal_keys_last_check`)

## Worked examples

Each is run against the real rule by `src/spec/spec.test.ts`: the result is what the code gives.

| Given | The rule gives |
|---|---|
| Typed "12.5", "12.50", "1,250", "29,4", "3.25 days". | `1, 1, 0, 1, 2` |
| 12.5 in a goal of whole numbers. | `12.5 has 1 decimal place, but this goal keeps whole numbers, so it would show as 13. Type 13, or set the goal’s Decimals to 1.` |
| The places a check-in offers to keep for 5.5, 5.25 and 1.23456 on a whole-number goal, and for 5. | `1, 2, 3, none` |
| 1250000, -12000 and 1250.5 shown. | `1,250,000, -12,000, 1,250.5` |
| A start of 10 signups and a target of 5,000. | `The target (5,000 signups) is over 100 times where it starts (10 signups). Is that right?` |
| 400, then 110, for the 30→75% goal: is each far outside its plan (`farOutside`, the plan’s width is 45)? Then what a check-in does with each: the goal is a share (its plan is within 0–100%), so over 100% is refused before anything is questioned. A growth goal from 30 to 75 in signups (not a share) given 400. | `far outside, not; refused, refused: It can’t be over 100%: this goal measures a share of something.; questioned: That’s far outside this goal’s plan (30 to 75 signups). Is 400 right?` |
| A queue wait goal, 14 → 3 min (lower is better), given a target of 999. | `direction: This makes higher better: the target (999 min) is now above the start (14 min). It was 14 min to 3 min, lower is better. [Yes, make higher better]` |
| The 30→75 goal given a target of 400, then of 90. | `far: The target of 400% is far outside the plan it replaces (30% to 75%). Status, progress and the forecast will all be judged against it. / fine` |
| In the demo workspace, Tariq turns the AI-assisted reviews north star (ns-ai) round (its target the same distance on the other side of its start), with a reason; then again, confirmed. | `asks first, nothing to save; ready to save` |

## Requirements

- `NO-SILENT-ROUNDING`: A number is never rounded quietly: one typed with more decimal places than its goal keeps is refused, with what it would show as, in the check-in, New goal, goal edit, the import and the AI tools. Letters in a number get one message everywhere, every number shown has its thousands grouped, and numbers far outside the plan are questioned, never refused.
- `SAME-NAMES`: Two goals may share a title and two people a name (the email is who someone is). Creating one warns; wherever both could be on screen, a goal shows its key and a person their team or job title beside the name, and people with the same initials get different avatar colours.

## Tests that check it

### [src/domain/numbers.test.ts](../../../src/domain/numbers.test.ts)

- no silent rounding › counts the decimal places a number was typed with
- no silent rounding › refuses a number with more decimal places than its goal keeps, and says what it would show as
- no silent rounding › refuses it in a check-in, as a code the screens and the import read
- no silent rounding › refuses it in New goal and goal edit, for start, target, limit, margin and plan numbers typed by hand
- no silent rounding › leaves a stored plan alone when editing: only numbers changed are judged
- no silent rounding › refuses it in the spreadsheet import and the AI tools, which share the bulk-change engine
- no silent rounding › reads a decimal comma as decimal places when an import works out a new goal’s decimals
- no silent rounding › keeps the demo workspace to its own rule: no number stored finer than its goal shows
- one message for letters in a number › says the same in the check-in, New goal, the workspace set-up and the import
- one message for letters in a number › gives an example at the goal’s decimal places: no decimal on a whole-number goal (deep review U10)
- thousand separators › groups the digits of every number shown
- plausibility: asked, never refused › asks about a check-in far outside the plan
- plausibility: asked, never refused › asks about a set-up number below zero for a time, money or percentage, a target a hundred times the start, or a billion
- plausibility: asked, never refused › asks it in an import without refusing the row, and saves once it is answered (C6)

### [src/domain/names.test.ts](../../../src/domain/names.test.ts)

- people with the same name › are allowed: the email is who someone is
- people with the same name › are told apart by team, else job title, else email, wherever both could be on screen
- people with the same name › get avatar colours that differ when their initials match
- people with the same name › can be set up together, with a note on the second one’s row
- people with the same name › can be added by spreadsheet, with a note
- goals with the same title › are allowed with a note when the team differs, and asked about when it is the same (C10)
- goals with the same title › show their key (or team) beside the title, and only when another goal has it
- one shortest name › holds a workspace, a goal and an outcome to the same minimum
